intent: Diagnose the selected thinking-enabled transfer configuration's live deadline exposure without changing the model condition or claiming release completion.

reported_staging_evidence.source: Release owner's Management API function_logs observation; not independently fetched by this auditor

independent_saved_timing_analysis.interpretation: The selected condition has an observed long tail beyond the live150-second envelope. Full-inventory concurrent fanout waits for its slowest target and increases exposure. These timings do not isolate model generation from provider/network queuing.

platform_verification.limits: Official documentation lists free worker wall clock150seconds, paid worker400seconds, and request idle timeout150seconds. Worker life can span multiple requests.
platform_verification.interpretation: A larger browser-test wait cannot extend a worker's wall clock. A paid worker alone also does not extend the documented idle-response deadline. Correlate the reported shutdown with the actual invocation before asserting which provider call caused it.

source_findings.finding: analyzeMessage launches one provider call per target with Promise.all and has no explicit fetch deadline. It applies one combined analysis only after every target response validates. A worker shutdown can discard all completed in-memory target responses.

The client caches only confirmed server completion and preserves failures. Each API request receives a fresh request_id. Retrying after an incomplete analysis can repeat every target call; the cache is not a per-target response journal.

recordProviderAttempt belongs to assessment generation, hardcodes its1200-token journal setting and expects assessment scope fields. analyzeMessage never calls it. It cannot be reused unchanged as an8000-token analysis journal.

live_schema_verification.tool: Supabase MCP execute_sql and get_project_url, read-only
live_schema_verification.scope_limit: MCP is bound to production and rejects project_id overrides. These are production definitions, not a claim that staging RPC bytes were inspected.
live_schema_verification.idempotence: apply_transfer_message_analysis_v1 obtains a message advisory transaction lock and checks analysis:<message_id> in private.learning_event_inbox. Applied/no_change markers return already_processed. Guard deferral is retained. This protects database effects after analysis; it does not reserve or dedupe the preceding provider calls.
live_schema_verification.existing_attempt_table: private.transfer_provider_attempts permits attempt_ordinal1 or2 only and has UNIQUE(request_id,attempt_ordinal). It is a two-attempt assessment journal, not an existing arbitrary-item durable transfer job/cache.

smallest_next_checks: Use existing staging invocation/gateway logs to correlate execution ID, request start, response status and shutdown, then read the message analysis marker and accepted events. Distinguish no response, client abandonment and a genuinely completed server analysis.

If the existing traces cannot identify the slow target, add minimal per-item start/finish/elapsed/status/finish_reason/usage/request-hash metadata around the unchanged provider request and one combined-completion log. Record IDs and timing rather than keys or learner text. No sampling or token-budget change is needed for this instrumentation.
Verify staging context/apply RPC definitions directly before relying on the production-confirmed message-idempotence properties.

smallest_contract_preserving_hardening.proposal: Give analysis provider work an explicit shared deadline below the confirmed live request/worker envelope, reserving time for error serialization or final persistence. Abort outstanding fetches and return the existing named retryable error contract when the deadline is exhausted. Keep temperature0/max_tokens8000/thinkingtrue and the complete target inventory unchanged.
smallest_contract_preserving_hardening.completion_rule: Do not apply partial inventory as analysis_complete, mark deferred success, or cache unfinished messages as completed. Retain validated model decisions; retryability must not become semantic outcome selection.
smallest_contract_preserving_hardening.limitation: This converts an opaque platform termination into a bounded recoverable failure. It does not guarantee successful completion of the observed long-tail condition and is insufficient by itself to declare the transfer release verified.
smallest_contract_preserving_hardening.next_scope_if_required: Reliable reuse across retries requires a separately reviewed durable per-item exact-request response journal or a worker/request arrangement that survives the measured latency. It must preserve complete-inventory application, current scope/state checks, Guard deferral, chronological message processing and final message dedupe. Existing RPC idempotence alone does not supply that architecture.

release_implication: Keep production promotion blocked on successful full-inventory staging completion and the affected lifecycle verification. Increasing only a test wait or silently reducing reasoning/token settings would not resolve the observed architectural deadline exposure.
